report.summary: The idle mDNS abort did not reproduce (fresh panel ran 2.5 min idle and stayed healthy), but a commissioned panel's reboot still crashes: a CPU 'Cache error' (unmapped PC 0xAFD6A25E) inside the Wi-Fi driver ~800 ms after the console reboot, so the previously failing stability scenario is not closed.

deviceInfo.bootTime: fresh boot reaches the console ~2.1 s after reset
deviceInfo.chip: ESP32-S31 rev v0.0, 2 cores, 16 MB flash, 16 MB PSRAM
deviceInfo.connectivity: no broker peer on the emulator (dials fail 'Host is unreachable'); onboarding SoftAP when unconfigured; station-only mode after commissioning
deviceInfo.crashes: 1 this session: CPU 'Cache error' (mcause 0x19) with PC=0xAFD6A25E inside ieee80211_getmgtframe ~800 ms after the console 'reboot' of a commissioned panel; emulator exit code 1
deviceInfo.freeHeap: ~12.55 MB free overall; internal DRAM ~50 KB free (20 KB largest); DMA-capable ~27 KB (16 KB largest)

notes: The mdns-critical fix appears effective: the fresh panel sat idle at the REPL for over 2.5 minutes with no stack-overflow hook (previous builds died 15-30 s in), and the steady-state idle trace is clean.

The new crash is not a stack overflow: it is a hard CPU fault ('Cache error', mcause 0x19) with PC 0xAFD6A25E — outside any mapped flash/IRAM region — raised inside the Wi-Fi driver's ieee80211_getmgtframe/ieee80211_send_probereq path right after the reboot. That is a code-execution fault in the emulated Wi-Fi stack, not a product handler misbehaving, and it did not occur on the fresh boot or after commissioning commands.

The code-review's finding that CONFIG_MDNS_TASK_STACK_SIZE never reaches the generated sdkconfig.h stands as a source observation; the runtime idle window above is consistent with mDNS simply not being the trigger for that window on this emulator, so the mdns overflow should still be re-tested on the real board rather than assumed fixed.

Non-fatal lines, not counted on their own: sdmmc_init_ocr 0x107 (no SD card), sccb_i2c transmit error then a correct ov3660 detection, 'i2s_common: GPIO 4/5 is not usable', 'gpio: conflict found for GPIO[7]', phy RF-calibration fallback, the emulator's failed-handshake warning for its virtual Wi-Fi client, and the usual Wi-Fi rate/power dump.
report.suggestedFix: The remaining configured-reboot failure is a CPU cache/permission fault inside the emulated Wi-Fi driver, not a product stack size: PC 0xAFD6A25E is not a valid code address and the backtrace lands in ieee80211_getmgtframe/ieee80211_send_probereq just after esp_wifi_start on a stored-credential boot. Either the product is starting the station while the driver is still bringing its own structures up, or the emulated driver faults on this sequence; separate the two by logging the Wi-Fi state transitions on a configured boot and, if needed, delaying the connect further (mqtt_net already waits 1 s after GOT_IP — the STA_START path itself is not debounced). Verify with three consecutive boots with stored credentials each reaching 'Console ready' and 'ZeroCode AI firmware started' and staying up 3 minutes.

tests.details: The fresh panel survived a 2.5-minute idle window after boot (uptime 3 s -> 53 s -> 100 s, all answered) with no stack-overflow hook; the mdns abort of the previous build did not reproduce in that window. NOTE: the code-review reports CONFIG_MDNS_TASK_STACK_SIZE absent from the generated header, so the fix may not be in the image — the pass here rests on the observed idle log, and this item should still be re-run on the real board.

tests.details: The boot after the console 'reboot' of the commissioned panel aborted with a CPU 'Cache error' (mcause 0x19, PC=0xAFD6A25E, an unmapped address) from inside the Wi-Fi driver (ieee80211_getmgtframe / ieee80211_send_probereq), ~800 ms in, just after the set_btn/boot_btn bindings; the emulator exited (code 1) and the panel stayed off. This is not the old sys_evt stack overflow — it is a code-execution fault on the configured-reboot path.
